How the farm works

Click an empty plot to plant. Click a growing crop to water; click a ripe crop to harvest. Crops only grow while wet. Turnips need 22 watered seconds; tomatoes need 36. The watering can holds 6 units. Visit the well to refill.

Gather wood and stone, craft at the bench, then place a device on an empty plot. Sprinklers water the surrounding 3 × 3 area every 8 seconds. Scarecrows protect crops within two tiles from birds that visit every 150 seconds. Sleep restores energy, regrows resources and ripens watered crops.

Both you and the helper use the same supplies. Sell harvests to buy seeds, or bring Ada three turnips for 50 coins and friendship. Farm changes save locally; a running program does not resume after reloading.

Mission guidance

Commands & language

This is a bounded C-style teaching language, not a full C compiler. Use int, float, double, bool, char; assignment; arithmetic; comparisons; if/else; for, while, do/while; and fixed arrays. User-defined functions and pointers are not supported.

plant(row, col); // optional third argument: "tomato"
water(row, col); harvest(row, col);
refill(); gather("wood"); gather("stone");
craft("sprinkler"); place("sprinkler", 1, 2);
craft("scarecrow"); place("scarecrow", 2, 4);
buy("turnip", 5); sell("turnip", 1);
deliver(); rest(); wait(3); move(6, 5);

// Sensors read the live farm and return numbers:
ripe(row, col); empty(row, col); wet(row, col);
water_left(); seeds("turnip"); stock("wood");
coins(); energy();

Rows: 0–2. Columns: 0–4. Execution is limited to 400 actions and 12,000 operations. Errors stop the helper; earlier changes remain. Mission starters are incomplete routines to develop in the actual field.
